steps.title: Bordeaux grapes
steps.body: Merlot is the most planted red, with Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Malbec, mostly in Bordeaux-style blends. They give medium to full-bodied wines with blackcurrant, plum, cedar and fresh acidity, more elegant than warmer New World examples. Merlot ripens more reliably than Cabernet here.

steps.title: Syrah and Chardonnay
steps.body: Syrah does very well: peppery, floral and medium-bodied, closer to the northern Rhône than to Barossa Shiraz. Chardonnay is Hawke's Bay's most planted grape overall, giving ripe yet fresh wines with stone fruit and citrus, often barrel-fermented. Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Gris also grow.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its style.
steps.explanation: Hawke's Bay is New Zealand's red heartland.

steps.body: Hawke's Bay Syrah is a good alternative to northern Rhône Syrah, with similar black pepper and violet.

steps.prompt: How is Hawke's Bay Syrah usually described?
steps.explanation: Its moderate climate gives a cooler style.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Chardonnay is the most planted grape overall
